subject: SummitCorp renewal: path to marketplace SKU + co-sell enablement
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@summitcorp.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@summitcorp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SummitCorp renewal: path to marketplace SKU + co-sell enablement

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Happy Friday — SummitCorp's annual renewal is coming up (license anniversary: 2026-09-30). I wanted to outline a low-friction path to move your billing to marketplace SKUs and enable the co-sell benefits the team discussed with Product a few weeks back. High-level: moving to marketplace simplifies PO/invoice flow for your procurement, unlocks partnering incentives (co-sell), and preserves your existing entitlements.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm procurement contact and any internal billing constraints
- Review the attached marketplace pricing workbook (SummitCorp_Marketplace_Pricing.xlsx) — shows 12/24-month options + EDP vs. standard
- If agreeable, we can provision the marketplace SKU mapping and issue a DocuSign amendment for signature (we can include a one-time conversion credit)

Quick notes on seller economics and timeline:
- We typically map your current subscription to a marketplace SKU and issue final direct invoice, then cutover to marketplace billing on the next term start
- Co-sell enablement (Microsoft/AWS partner motions) requires a short partner form + a co-sell acceptance from your side — we can handle the partner paperwork once procurement signs off

Questions for you: who in procurement owns marketplace enrollments? Is there a preferred channel (AWS Marketplace / Azure Marketplace / direct invoice through GCP) you want to prioritize? Also FYI attaching a draft MAP (RDW_SummitCorp_MAP_v2.pdf) with suggested conversion credit.

I’ll loop in Grace and Karthik for finance/legal alignment once we have the procurement point of contact.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Attachments: SummitCorp_Marketplace_Pricing.xlsx, RDW_SummitCorp_MAP_v2.pdf

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@summitcorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@summitcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitCorp renewal: path to marketplace SKU + co-sell enablement

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the note. Procurement here — happy to explore marketplace but a few things before we proceed:
1) Will we be able to keep the same SKUs/features? Any functional differences with the marketplace SKU mapping?
2) Can you confirm timing for final invoice cutover and whether our legal needs to review a new amendment?
3) We need SOC 2 and data residency proof for our compliance team — do you have the latest evidence pack?
4) What does the conversion credit look like (one-time credit vs. recurring discount)?

If you can send a short MAP and sample amendment we can route this internally. My procurement lead (Tom) will be the approver for marketplace switches.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of Procurement — SummitCorp
aisha.patel@summitcorp.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: SummitCorp marketplace conversion proposal (prep for Aisha)

Grace / Karthik —

Internal note before I respond to procurement: Aisha asked the right questions. I recommend the following posture for negotiation:
- Offer a one-time marketplace conversion credit equal to 10% of the ARR if they commit to a 12-month marketplace term (applies only to first marketplace-billed term).
- Keep the feature parity by mapping current entitlements 1:1 to marketplace SKUs (no functional changes).
- Provide the SOC 2 evidence pack and a short amendment template for legal review (attach RDW_SummitCorp_MAP_v2.pdf).

Draft reply will: attach the SOC2 link, clarify cutover timing (final direct invoice at current term end, marketplace from next term start), and propose the DocuSign amendment with the 10% one-time credit. If legal wants to escalate the wording, we can route to Jane in Legal; finance is ok with the credit as a one-off.

I’ll send the external reply in ~30 minutes unless you want changes.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@summitcorp.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@summitcorp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitCorp renewal: path to marketplace SKU + co-sell enablement

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks for the quick reply and the questions — answered inline below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Feature parity: we will map your current entitlements 1:1 to marketplace SKUs. There are no functional differences; this is strictly a billing channel change.

2) Timing & amendment: final direct invoice runs through the current term (ends 2026-09-30). Marketplace billing would be active from 2026-10-01 onward. Attached is a short amendment (RDW_SummitCorp_MAP_v2.pdf) that legal can review — it limits the credit to the first marketplace term and captures the SKU mapping.

3) Compliance evidence: SOC 2 and data residency documents are available here: https://redwood-internal.example.com/evidence/summitcorp-soc2 (please let me know if you need a PDF pack instead).

4) Conversion credit: we propose a one-time credit equal to 10% of the ARR applied to the first marketplace-billed invoice. If SummitCorp can commit to a 24-month marketplace term we can consider structuring a multi-term discount as an alternative.

Next steps:
- If this looks good, please confirm procurement sign-off and I’ll send the DocuSign amendment for signature: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/summitcorp-sept-renewal
- Once signed, we’ll coordinate the SKU entitlements mapping and schedule a short ops call to validate billing fields (PO number, legal entity for marketplace subscriptions).

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the amendment.

Best regards,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
